title: Why have a bank account?
blurb: Ravi keeps his savings in a tin. Find out what can go wrong, and what a bank account does differently.
t1.title: The tin under the bed
t1.hook: Ravi keeps {tin} of savings in a tin under his bed. One monsoon night the roof leaks and {damaged} of the notes are ruined.
t1.define: A **bank account** is a safe place to keep money. The bank records every rupee you put in or take out.
t1.analogy: A bank is like a strong cupboard with a watchman and a notebook. Your money is locked away, and every rupee is written down.
q1.prompt: Ravi had {tin} in the tin. {damaged} was ruined by water. How much is left? Type a number in rupees.
q1.hint: Take away what was ruined from what he had.
q2.prompt: Which of these is a real risk of keeping all your savings as cash at home?
q2.hint: Think about water, fire, theft and loss.
q2.explain: Cash at home can be lost, stolen or damaged, and nobody can get it back for you.
q2.opt.a: It can be lost, stolen or damaged
t2.title: Records and access
t2.define: A bank keeps a **record** of every deposit and every withdrawal. You can look back and see where your money went.
t2.note: Many scholarships and salaries are paid straight into a bank account. Without one, you may have to collect cash in person.
q3.prompt: Meena wants to know how much she spent on bus fares last month. What helps her most?
q3.hint: Which one keeps a written list of every rupee in and out?
q3.explain: The bank record lists every deposit and withdrawal, so she can add up the bus fares.
q3.opt.b: Counting the notes in her purse
q4.prompt: Asha's college scholarship is paid by transfer, not cash. What does she need?
q4.hint: The money has to arrive somewhere with her name on it.
q4.explain: A transfer needs an account with her name. The scholarship arrives there safely.
q4.opt.a: A bank account in her name
t3.title: Money that grows a little
t3.define: The bank uses the money people keep with it. In return it pays you **interest**: a small extra amount, added to your account.
t3.formula: Interest = balance × rate × years. Here the rate is a yearly rate as a fraction, so 3% means 0.03.
t3.steps.1: Asha keeps {exBal} in a savings account.
t3.steps.2: The yearly rate is {rate}, and she keeps it for {years1} year.
q5.prompt: Meena keeps {qBal} in her account for {years1} year at {rate} a year. How much interest does she earn? Type a number in rupees.
q5.hint: Multiply the balance by the rate and by the years.
q6.prompt: What is the interest on a savings account?
q6.hint: Who pays whom? Read the card again.
q6.explain: Interest is paid to you by the bank for keeping your money with it. It is not a fee.
q6.opt.b: A fee you pay every year
q6.fb.b: Interest comes to you, not from you. A fee is something you pay. Interest is something you receive.
t4.title: Lab: balance and time
t4.explore: Open the lab. Drag the sliders to change the balance and the years, and watch the interest.
q7.prompt: In the lab, set the balance to {labBal} and the years to {labYears}. How much interest is earned? Type a number in rupees.
q7.hint: Use the sliders and read the interest earned.
q8.prompt: At the same rate for a year, who earns more interest: someone with {loBal} or someone with {hiBal}?
q8.hint: Try both balances in the lab.
q8.explain: A bigger balance earns more interest at the same rate and time.
t5.title: Small amounts add up
t5.define: You do not need a lot to begin. Putting aside a small amount each month builds a real pile over time.
t5.steps.1: Asha puts {exMonthly} into her account each month.
t5.steps.2: After {exMonths} months she has put in {exSaved}.
t5.steps.3: The bank record shows each deposit, so she can see it grow.
t5.mistake: Some people think bank accounts are only for people with lots of money. Many accounts can be opened with a small amount, or none at all.
q9.prompt: Ravi puts {saveMonthly} into his account every month for {saveMonths} months. How much has he put in? Type a number in rupees.
q9.hint: Multiply the monthly amount by the number of months.
q10.prompt: Meena only has {tiny} to start with. What is true?
q10.hint: Remember the note about small amounts.
q10.explain: Many accounts accept small amounts, and some need no starting money. You can add more later.
q10.opt.a: A small amount can still be saved in an account
q10.opt.b: Banks refuse anyone with small savings
q10.fb.b: Banks do not only want big savers. Many accounts start with a small amount or none.
q10.opt.c: She must wait until she is rich
q10.opt.d: Interest only works on big amounts
glossary.bank_account.def: A safe place at a bank where your money is kept and recorded.
glossary.bank_interest.def: Extra money the bank pays you for keeping your money with it.
glossary.bank_balance.def: The amount of money in your account right now.
